items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1971-04-20
items.q: I had a band. ... Eddie Atkins on trombone.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. I guess I better get another reel of tape. Find it. Yeah. Because I've heard about those bands, you know. Like that.

You know, Eddie played nice man, good mandolin. Played guitar, banjo. And I heard he was playing bass. And boy, she played nice bass, you see, yeah? You know, last time, the other night I got to hear him. She could play nice bass. He got good bass, too.
Yeah, he does all right for a young man, I guess. Right? Yeah, he's doing a job.

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1957-04-16
items.q: I used to have Manuel, Teo, Frankie Enya, see, and, uh, Eddie Atkins on some bones.

ctx.x: Then the next band went, Big Eye Lewy. He come along. Big Eye Lewy was with Freddie and, uh, and-and-and-and George Backe was with, uh, And, uh, George Fields was with Manuel. Then when I was at the Dreamland, I went to Wake Down and Peekin for Dan Jackson, and I used to have Manuel, Teo, Frankie Enya, see, and, uh, Eddie Atkins on some bones.

items.title: 68090_Ed Garland oral history interview
items.q: And I played out there with him. And he had Manuel Perez played trumpet. Eddie Atkins playing trombone.

ctx.x: And I played out there with him. And he had Manuel Perez played trumpet. Eddie Atkins playing trombone. Lorenzo To playing clarinet.
